pois.name: Bismarck: main hull
pois.note: Repositioned 2026-09 to the H.M.S. Hood Association's 2001 expedition fix ('vicinity of 4809N 01607W' = 48.15N, 16.117W), the most specific sourced coordinate found, and corroborated by a third published figure (48°09'N 016°07'W) distinct from Wikipedia's rounded infobox (48°10'N 16°12'W). The tile has been regenerated around this point. depth_m 4213 sits ~5 m above this tile's own terrain reading of 4,218.5 m here, for a scan target at roughly deck height -- but that terrain reading is itself ~570 m shallower than the commonly published wreck depth (4,790-4,791 m): this point sits on the upper flank of the seamount, closer to its summit (terrain shoals to ~4,024 m about 3 km north-east), not at the depth the hull is reported to have finally settled at after sliding downslope. We did not shift the coordinate further to force a depth match -- that would fabricate precision no source supports -- so this gap is reported rather than hidden; see sources.md. Confidence is medium because of this unresolved depth-vs-terrain gap, not because the ship's identity or general condition is in doubt.

pois.name: Detached main gun turrets
pois.note: Bismarck's four main-battery turrets broke free of their barbettes, being unbolted from below, and dropped separately during the sinking; Ballard's 1989 survey located only one, upside-down and half-buried, and could not find the other three. Later surveys (Magellan/Parks Stephenson, 2019) mapped more of the debris field, roughly a line of turret positions along the slope. No public coordinates were found for the individual turrets, so this marker is an illustrative placement roughly 1.2 km up-slope (north-east, toward the seamount summit) of the reconstructed hull -- consistent with published accounts that the turrets struck the seamount first and triggered the landslide that carried the hull further downslope -- not a surveyed position, hence the low confidence. Repositioned 2026-09 along with the hull; see sources.md.

pois.name: Battle damage: shell and torpedo hits
pois.note: Marks the historical question, not a single surveyed feature: whether British shellfire and torpedoes, or the crew's own scuttling charges, caused the final sinking. kbismarck.com's survey notes describe the hull as in surprisingly good condition given the battering it took, with the stern the most heavily damaged section. Illustrative placement near the hull; moved 2026-09 with the hull to the sourced wreck position (see sources.md).

pois.name: The seamount flank
pois.note: Real survey data, repositioned 2026-09 with the wreck: this tile's terrain shoals from 4,218.5 m at the hull to about 4,182 m here, roughly 500 m up-slope (north-east) toward the seamount summit (which reaches ~4,024 m about 3 km further along the same line). Published accounts describe the real debris trail as about 1 km long down a much steeper (~14.5 degree) slope, formed when the turrets hit the seamount first and triggered a landslide that carried the hull further down -- so this point sits between the turret-debris marker (further up-slope) and the hull (down-slope), on the same real slope. This tile's grid, built from GMRT's coarser global (GEBCO-derived) fill rather than a dedicated survey of the wreck site, is far too coarse to resolve the true trail or slope angle -- what you scan here is real but smoothed terrain, not the skid mark itself.

pois.name: Memorial marker
pois.note: A respectful marker near the hull, not a surveyed structure or a prop. Of Bismarck's crew of 2,221, only around 114 were rescued; roughly 2,100 died. This game has no salvage, collection or loot of any kind at any site.
